questions.stem: A user wants to extend the Windows paging file to use more virtual memory. Which Control Panel path leads there?

choices.text: System > Advanced System Settings > Performance > Advanced > Virtual Memory
Programs and Features > Turn Windows features on or off

questions.explanation: Virtual memory (paging file) settings are deep in System > Advanced System Settings.
questions.trap: Power Options is for sleep / hibernate, not paging.

questions.stem: A laptop user closes the lid before commuting home but the battery is almost always dead when they arrive. Which power state should they switch to?
questions.explanation: Hibernate writes state to disk and uses no power, so the laptop survives long idle periods without battery drain.
questions.trap: Sleep and Standby both keep state in RAM and continue to drain battery.

questions.stem: Where in the Control Panel do you enable / disable IIS, Hyper-V, or Windows Subsystem for Linux?

choices.text: Programs and Features > Turn Windows features on or off

questions.explanation: Windows components like IIS, Hyper-V, WSL are toggled via 'Turn Windows features on or off' in the Programs and Features applet.
questions.trap: (d) Settings > Apps > Optional Features manages downloadable language packs and small features, not the major Windows roles.

questions.stem: Windows Update reboots a user's PC during important client meetings. What setting addresses this without disabling updates?

choices.text: Set Active Hours in Windows Update settings

questions.explanation: Active Hours tells Windows Update not to reboot during the configured workday window. Updates still download and install around those hours.
questions.trap: (d) metered connection delays some downloads but doesn't fully solve the reboot timing problem.

questions.stem: A user reports their Mail icon is missing from the Control Panel. What is the MOST likely cause?

choices.text: Windows 11 removed the Mail applet from Control Panel
The user is not in the Administrators group
No supported email client (e.g. Outlook) is installed
Mail was disabled via Group Policy

questions.explanation: The Mail applet only appears in Control Panel once a supported email client is installed (typically Outlook).
questions.trap: Group Policy CAN hide it but the most common everyday cause is simply that Outlook isn't installed.

questions.stem: A technician needs to see hidden system files in File Explorer. Which Control Panel applet contains this setting?
questions.explanation: Show / hide hidden files and 'hide file extensions' are both on the View tab of File Explorer Options.
questions.trap: Indexing Options changes what is searched, not what is shown.

questions.stem: Match each task to the correct Control Panel applet.
questions.explanation: Knowing which applet owns which task is the core of 1.6.

questions.stem: Which statements about Windows power options are TRUE? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Hibernate writes state to disk and requires no power
Sleep keeps state in RAM and requires constant power
Fast Startup performs a complete shutdown then a quick boot
You can configure what happens when the laptop lid closes

questions.explanation: Hibernate uses disk (a), Sleep uses RAM (b), and lid behavior is configurable (d). Fast Startup does NOT perform a full shutdown; it hibernates the kernel.
questions.trap: (c) sounds right but is wrong. Fast Startup avoids the full shutdown - that's what makes it 'fast'.
